builder_plan.scenario: Your coding assistant makes changes that still need substantial repair before merging.
builder_plan.change: Try the technique on held-out issues from a repository with reliable tests.
builder_plan.baseline: The same coding agent, repository snapshot, tools, and token budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct patches, regression failures, human repair time, and total cost per accepted change.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Can LLM Agents Be Forward-Deployed Engineers? Requirement Discovery and Delivery for Enterprise Text-to-SQL
summary: The method replaces manual requirements engineering and post-training recipe design with a semi-automated agent pipeline, inserting human checkpoints to validate discovered criteria before execution. It costs additional infrastructure complexity for the agent harness, human review hours for requirement validation, and implementation overhead for explicit experiment-environment specifications. After adoption, unreliable execution can still cause three-quarters of delivery attempts to fail acceptance criteria, while incomplete discovery may omit or misrepresent critical constraints such as hardware budgets and data permissions.
rationale: The approach uses only third-party APIs or open-weight models and mandates human oversight to mitigate the demonstrated 75% delivery failure rate, fitting constrained infrastructure while requiring validation against the team's specific text-to-SQL workload.

claims.statement: The method replaces manual requirements engineering and post-training recipe design with a semi-automated agent pipeline, inserting human checkpoints to validate discovered criteria before execution. It costs additional infrastructure complexity for the agent harness, human review hours for requirement validation, and implementation overhead for explicit experiment-environment specifications. After adoption, unreliable execution can still cause three-quarters of delivery attempts to fail acceptance criteria, while incomplete discovery may omit or misrepresent critical constraints such as hardware budgets and data permissions.
The strongest models discover over 80% of withheld customer requirements, but only 25% of coding-agent configurations pass all acceptance criteria in the delivery phase.
